## Setup

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(magrittr)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
library(collections)
library(zoo)
library(maps)
library(here)
```

```{r load-data}
# Load child care data
childcare_data <- read_csv(here("cap_ccaccess_2025_revised_02282026.csv"))

# Dataframe attributes
colnames(childcare_data)
unique(childcare_data$state_name)
```

---

## Load FORHP Dataset

Download the Rural Health Areas Data Set from HRSA:
<https://www.hrsa.gov/rural-health/about-us/what-is-rural/data-files>

```{r load-forhp}
forhp_df <- read_excel(here("rural-health-areas-data-set.xlsx"), sheet = 3)

# Data checks
colnames(forhp_df)
## should read [1] "FIPS_2023" "State" "State_FIPS" "County_2023" "County_Name_2023" [6] "County_Eligibility"

# Number of counties classified as rural, nationwide
length(forhp_df$County_Name_2023[forhp_df$County_Eligibility == 'Not Fully FORHP Rural']) ## should be 923
length(forhp_df$County_Name_2023[forhp_df$County_Eligibility == 'Fully FORHP Rural'])     ## should be 2316
```

```{r forhp-by-state}
# Number of counties classified as rural, by state
state_filter <- 'XX'  ### Change 'XX' to state abbreviation of interest ###

length(forhp_df$County_Name_2023[
  (forhp_df$State == state_filter) &
  (forhp_df$County_Eligibility == 'Not Fully FORHP Rural')
]) # XXX not fully rural counties in state XX

length(forhp_df$County_Name_2023[
  (forhp_df$State == state_filter) &
  (forhp_df$County_Eligibility == 'Fully FORHP Rural')
]) # XXX fully rural counties in state XX
```

---

## Merge Datasets

```{r merge-forhp}
# Join HRSA data with child care data.
# Note: special characters in county names (e.g. ñ in NM) are corrected before
# merging; Puerto Rico is filtered out as it doesn't exist in the cap_ccaccess data.
joined_rural <- childcare_data %>%
  mutate(county_name = str_replace_all(county_name, 'Ã±', "ñ")) %>%
  filter(state_abbrv != 'PR')

joined_rural <- left_join(
  joined_rural, forhp_df,
  by = c('county_fips' = 'FIPS_2023',
         'state_abbrv' = 'State',
         'county_name' = 'County_Name_2023')
)

unique(joined_rural$County_Eligibility)
## double-checking no unexpected NAs created by merge
## should read [1] "Not Fully FORHP Rural" "Fully FORHP Rural" NA

# Create rural binary
joined_rural %<>%
  mutate(rural = ifelse(County_Eligibility == 'Fully FORHP Rural', 1, 0))
```

---

## Descriptive Statistics: FORHP Rurality

```{r forhp-descriptives}
rural     <- length(joined_rural$rural[joined_rural$rural == 1]) # 357,998 synth families in fully rural county
not_rural <- length(joined_rural$rural[joined_rural$rural == 0]) # 1,927,168 synth families in not fully rural county

rural     / length(joined_rural$county_name) * 100 ## should read [1] 15.69383
not_rural / length(joined_rural$county_name) * 100 ## should read [1] 84.48271
```

## Summarise Supply by Rurality

```{r supply-by-rurality-national}
# By rurality, nationwide
cap_ccaccess_grpd_rural <- joined_rural %>%
  group_by(rural, state_name) %>%
  summarize(
    avg_adj_supply      = mean(adj_supply),
    avg_adj_supply_fcc  = mean(adj_supply_fcc),
    avg_adj_supply_ccc  = mean(adj_supply_ccc),
    avg_adj_supply_hs   = mean(adj_supply_hs),
    avg_adj_supply_prek = mean(adj_supply_prek)
  )

view(cap_ccaccess_grpd_rural)
```

```{r supply-by-rurality-state}
# By rurality, by state
cap_ccaccess_grpd_rural <- joined_rural %>%
  group_by(rural, state_name) %>%
  summarize(
    avg_adj_supply      = mean(adj_supply),
    avg_adj_supply_fcc  = mean(adj_supply_fcc),
    avg_adj_supply_ccc  = mean(adj_supply_ccc),
    avg_adj_supply_hs   = mean(adj_supply_hs),
    avg_adj_supply_prek = mean(adj_supply_prek)
  )
```

## Load NCHS Urban-Rural Classification

```{r load-nchs}
nchs_df <- read_csv(here("data-table.csv"))

nchs_df %<>%
  separate_wider_delim(`2023 Code`, ' - ', names = c('urb_code', 'urb_category')) %>%
  mutate(urb_code = as.numeric(urb_code))

joined_rural <- left_join(
  joined_rural, nchs_df,
  by = c('county_fips' = 'Location', 'state_abbrv' = 'State')
)

unique(joined_rural$urb_category)
## should read [1] "Medium metro" "Small metro" "Micropolitan" "Large fringe metro"
##             [5] "Noncore" "Large central metro" NA
```

---

## Clean Master Dataframe

```{r clean-columns}
# Remove clutter columns from FORHP and NCHS joins.
# Fixed: original script had two near-identical select() calls; the second
# (referencing state_fips) was a duplicate that would silently fail once
# State_FIPS was already dropped. Consolidated into a single call.
joined_rural %<>%
  select(-c('State_FIPS', 'County_2023', 'FullGeoName', 'County_name'))
```

## Desert Rates by Urban/Rural Type

```{r desert-by-urbcode}
# Desert rates by urban code, using the 0.33 threshold
joined_rural %>%
  group_by(urb_code, urb_category) %>%
  summarise(
    total_obs    = n(),
    desert_count = sum(adj_supply < 0.33, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_desert   = (desert_count / total_obs) * 100
  )

## Expected output:
# urb_code urb_category        total_obs desert_count pct_desert
# 1        1 Large central metro    722694       251585       34.8
# 2        2 Large fringe metro     567149       250285       44.1
# 3        3 Medium metro           484679       234698       48.4
# 4        4 Small metro            195089       105313       54.0
# 5        5 Micropolitan           184664       111709       60.5
# 6        6 Noncore                113840        80619       70.8
# 7       NA NA                      13024        13024      100.0
```

```{r desert-by-state-urbcode}
# Breakdown by state and urban category
joined_rural %>%
  filter(!is.na(urb_code)) %>%
  group_by(state_name, urb_code, urb_category) %>%
  summarise(
    total_obs    = n(),
    desert_count = sum(adj_supply < 0.33, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_desert   = (desert_count / total_obs) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(state_name, urb_code)
```

## State/Classification Filter Function

Use this function to filter the dataset to an individual state by either FORHP or NCHS classification.

Set `classification` to either:

- `'rural'` — FORHP classification
- `'urb_code'` — NCHS classification

```{r filter-function}
classification <- 'urb_code' # change to 'rural' or 'urb_code'

filt_state_code <- function(df, state = '', classification = '') {
  if (length(state) > 0) {
    df <- df %>%
      filter(state_name == state)
  }

  # Fixed: original function grouped by .data[[code]], but the argument
  # is named classification, not code. Corrected to .data[[classification]].
  agg_df <- df %>%
    group_by(.data[[classification]], state_name) %>%
    summarize(
      syn_families        = n(),               # number of synth families in state by classification
      avg_adj_supply      = mean(adj_supply),
      avg_adj_supply_fcc  = mean(adj_supply_fcc),
      avg_adj_supply_ccc  = mean(adj_supply_ccc),
      avg_adj_supply_hs   = mean(adj_supply_hs),
      avg_adj_supply_prek = mean(adj_supply_prek)
    )

  return(agg_df)
}
```
